title: Safe Deposit Boxes: Annual Rent, Branch Pricing and Lease Renewal
content:
Rent for the bank's Safe Deposit Boxes is an annual charge that depends on two things: the size of the box and the branch whose vault holds it. This page sets out the price list and how the yearly amount billed to the lessee is worked out.

## Rental year and renewal

Each rental year runs 12 months for every size. Rent for a year is charged once, in advance, on the rent due date. For every size the lease renews by itself at the close of each term, so a new rental year, with its own rent charge, follows on its own.

| Box size | Base annual rent (USD) | Term in months | Renews automatically |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3x5 Safe Deposit Box | 65.00 | 12 | Yes |
| 3x10 Safe Deposit Box | 85.00 | 12 | Yes |
| 5x10 Safe Deposit Box | 120.00 | 12 | Yes |
| 10x10 Safe Deposit Box | 175.00 | 12 | Yes |
| 10x15 Safe Deposit Box | 240.00 | 12 | Yes |
| 10x20 Safe Deposit Box | 325.00 | 12 | Yes |

## Branch adjustment

The base rent is raised or lowered by a percentage that depends on the branch where the rental sits. The same percentages apply to all six sizes.

| Branch | Adjustment to base rent |
|---|---|
| Greensboro Main Office | none (0 percent) |
| Winston-Salem Reynolda Road | none (0 percent) |
| Charlotte SouthPark | raised by 15 percent |
| Raleigh North Hills | raised by 10 percent |
| Greenville Main Street | none (0 percent) |
| Roanoke Market Square | lowered by 5 percent |

## How the yearly charge is defined

1. **Gross rent** is the base annual rent for the size, increased or decreased by the branch's adjustment percentage applied to that base, and then rounded half-up to the nearest cent.
2. **Net rent**, the amount actually charged for the year, is the gross rent from the line above reduced by the one discount percentage selected for that rental, with the result again rounded half-up to the nearest cent. The figure the discount reduces is therefore the rounded gross rent for the rental's branch. Where no discount applies, net rent equals gross rent in amount.

Only a single discount percentage ever enters this calculation for a given rental year.

## Worked example (hypothetical discount)

A 3x5 Safe Deposit Box at Charlotte SouthPark, with a hypothetical discount of 30 percent chosen purely to show the rounding:

- Gross rent: 65.00 raised by 15 percent gives 74.75, already a whole number of cents.
- Net rent: 74.75 reduced by 30 percent gives 52.325, which rounds half-up to 52.33.

The same box at Roanoke Market Square with no discount: 65.00 lowered by 5 percent gives a gross rent of 61.75, and a net rent of 61.75.

## Points of judgement

- *Which figure does a discount reduce?* The gross rent, that is, the base rent already adjusted for the branch and rounded to the cent.
- *Is rent billed monthly?* No. It is billed once per rental year, ahead of the year it pays for.
